- scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh:285-346 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The post-wait `followup-guard` call is now unconditional, so one step runs the guard twice (review_enable_auto_merge.sh:285 and :344), but the API-budget paragraph in the helper's header (scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:98-102) still counts the reads for a single call.
  WHY: An API-budget audit that trusts the header under-counts real usage by up to 2x, including a redundant second `/user` read; both reviewers rated it NIT and state it is not a runtime failure, because the double read is the intended TOCTOU fix.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:96-102 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The header's followup-guard API budget is written per invocation ("one head-filtered pulls listing, one /user read, one paginated parent comments read, at most one paginated read of this PR's comments ... and at most one comment"), but the "Enable auto-merge on PR" step now always invokes the mode twice (scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh:285 and scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh:344).
  WHY: For follow-up PRs whose base is neither the default branch nor an integration branch, one step run issues twice the published reads (2 pulls listings, 2 /user reads, 2 parent-comment listings, up to 2 PR-comment reads), so a §15 audit under-counts usage against the shared PAT rate limit; rated NIT.
- scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh:265-344 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Each guard invocation does its own `/user` identity read (scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:901-908), so the second call at line 344 repeats a read the first call already made in the same step.
  WHY: Not a failure; the only cost is one redundant GET /user per auto-merge enablement step for follow-up-shaped PRs (NIT).

The judge merge calls (including 2571-2573 and 2664-2666) and the deterministic-skip calls (1431, 1468) are unguarded.
